scope: Technical planning evidence after the first verified BNCI2014-001 run; no new model downloads or website publication in this review

assessment.near_term_primary_bottleneck: Protocol validity and model-specific adaptation; current global-mean pilot must not be interpreted as each foundation model's general capability
assessment.data_bottleneck: Independent subject/dataset/device coverage and known pretraining overlap, rather than raw file volume
assessment.model_count: Enough candidate families for a 3-4-family research preview; only LaBraM and EEGPT have been executed here
assessment.compute: Current two-model frozen-probe MI run fits M5/32GiB; do not extrapolate its runtime to full fine-tuning, larger models or sleep/clinical datasets
assessment.product_risk: Existing open EEG benchmarking frameworks already provide broad model/task coverage; sustained user value needs validation

current_framework_evidence.name: NeuralBench
current_framework_evidence.observed_readme_claim: 36 EEG tasks, 6 EEG foundation models and 8 task-specific models; versioned Core and Full suites
current_framework_evidence.implication: Prefer selective reuse of audited adapters/protocols over rebuilding a broad framework or downloading all datasets

current_framework_evidence.name: EEG-FM-Bench
current_framework_evidence.observed_readme_claim: 14 datasets, 10 paradigms; lists BENDR, BIOT, CBraMod, EEGPT, LaBraM, CSBrain and REVE, separately from general time-series models

current_framework_evidence.name: Are EEG Foundation Models Worth It?
current_framework_evidence.evidence_scope: ICLR 2026 abstract reports weak linear probing and task-dependent performance; not a replication or causal explanation of our pilot scores

candidate_additions.name: CBraMod
candidate_additions.weights_status: Official README links pretrained weights; not downloaded or executed here
candidate_additions.reason: Official example uses 22 channels and four 200-sample temporal patches
candidate_additions.pretraining_overlap: Disclosed TUEG pretraining; exact checkpoint/corpus audit remains required

candidate_additions.name: REVE
candidate_additions.weights_status: Official pretrained and BCIC-IV-2a linear-probe entrypoints found; not downloaded or executed here
candidate_additions.pretraining_overlap: unknown for BNCI pending precise pretraining list inspection

candidate_additions.name: LUNA
candidate_additions.weights_status: Official model card inspected by subagent; not downloaded or executed here
candidate_additions.pretraining_overlap: unknown for BNCI; task adaptation and checkpoint terms need inspection

proposed_sequence: Preserve pilot; predeclare an adapter/readout comparison and add a randomly initialized backbone control plus EEGNet and/or a Riemannian baseline. Select hyperparameters only within training folds. Treat already inspected BNCI scores as development evidence.
Download and strictly validate CBraMod, then evaluate under a named protocol. Keep REVE optional until access, overlap and adapter checks pass.
Add a fixed Sleep-EDF SC cohort and subject-disjoint sleep scoring with sleep-specific preprocessing, plus an independently selected MI dataset for external confirmation as feasible.

Release a research preview with explicit task/protocol tables, model/data cards, per-subject uncertainty, resource measurements and reproducible evidence. Aim for 3-4 model families and two task types; show unsupported combinations honestly.
Add fixed low-channel and low-label comparisons on public data; distinguish simulations from 1-2-person cap integration demonstrations. Validate recurring user demand before broad clinical expansion.
planning_time: Approximately 1-2 weeks of engineering work for the proposed preview, conditional on checkpoint compatibility and protocol review; not a measured training-time estimate or scheduled background job
